newsitem.title: BRAZIL: COCOA--Confusion reigns over Bahia arrivals.
newsitem.headline: COCOA--Confusion reigns over Bahia arrivals.

text.p: Bahia cocoa traders said they are unsure whether this year's arrivals figures, which are used as a measure of the crop progress, would be revised following recent distortions.

The figures, which register the number of bags received by shippers and grinders in Bahia from farmers, were not announced during a six-week period earlier this year and later suffered a readjustment due to double-counting.
Both problems will make comparisons meaningless next year unless revisions are made, traders said.
Figures came to a halt following the end of the fifth week of the 1996/7 crop in June due to the re-organisation of the Brazil Cocoa Trade Commission (Comcauba), which issues them, traders said.
The cumulative total at the time was 321,636 60-kilo bags, compared to 150,409 bags at the same stage of the 1995/6 crop.
Comcauba began issuing the figures again at the end of July, with a figure of 811,073 bags for the six weeks ending July 28, an average of 115,867 for each of the missing weeks.
Figures have since come out regularly with the weekly total ranging between 25,000 and 60,000 bags.
However, further confusion was created when a figure of 209,329 bags was announced for the week ending September 22, the 19th week of the crop season.
Traders said that the high figure was due to a company that is not a Comcauba member registering several weeks' worth of arrivals all in one go.

A few days later, Comcauba reduced the figure for the 19th week from 209,329 to 159,897 after discovering that some of the bags had been double counted. This reduced the cumulative total after 20 weeks to 1,594,003 bags.

Traders said, however, that unless the figures for the preceeding weeks are revised to allow for the late declaration, it will not be possible next year to make meaningful comparisons with the progress of this year's crop.
Comcauba still has to elect a new president and a spokesman said he could not say whether an eventual revision would take place.
"I don't know what Comcauba are going to do," said a trader.
Another conflict is caused by the fact that the 1996/7 crop year began one week later than the previous year.

The current cumulative total of 1,691,242, at the end of the week-ending September 29, was achieved in 21 weeks. It is being compared by Comcauba with last year's cumulative total of 1,021,860, achieved in 22 weeks. Both figures represent the final total for their crop year's respective midcrops.
The 1996/7 main crop begins this week and is expected to yield between 1.0 and 1.1 million bags.
